description:
Galactic Wardens is building health monitoring software for astronauts on space missions in the NASA Space Apps Challenge. We’re seeking UI/UX designers, storytellers, and developers to join our team and create tools that keep crews safe and healthy beyond Earth.

✨Let’s protect the explorers of the final frontier together. More info given in r dc.
summary:
Galden is an advanced offline-first 3D bio-telemetry software and multi-agent health monitoring suite engineered for astronauts on long-duration space missions. To address the critical physiological challenges of microgravity, the system continuously tracks key biomarkers and models musculoskeletal degradation—including bone mineral density loss and associated molecular pathways like sclerostin and RANKL.

Operating 100% locally and offline without requiring external API keys or continuous cloud connectivity, Galden guarantees uninterrupted data security, real-time diagnostics, and localized intelligence during deep-space communication blackouts.
This system is vital because prolonged spaceflight accelerates physiological decline, posing severe risks to astronaut health. By providing autonomous, multi-agent predictive analytics and immediate health status assessments directly on-board, Galden eliminates reliance on Earth-based ground control. It empowers crew members with actionable insights to execute proactive medical countermeasures, ultimately safeguarding astronaut well-being and ensuring mission success for future interplanetary exploration.
details:
What does it do and how does it work?

Galden is an offline-first, 3D bio-telemetry visualization and multi-agent AI health monitoring system designed for astronauts on long-duration space missions.

Telemetry & Biomarker Tracking: It ingests physiological data and models musculoskeletal changes caused by microgravity, specifically tracking bone mineral density (BMD) loss and molecular indicators such as sclerostin and RANKL pathways.

Local Multi-Agent Architecture: Instead of relying on cloud APIs, Galden runs a localized, multi-agent AI system directly on onboard hardware. Specialized AI agents analyze incoming telemetry, cross-reference physiological baselines with spaceflight medical datasets (such as NASA OSDR and HRP data), and flag early signs of tissue degradation or health anomalies.

Interactive 3D Interface: The software renders real-time physiological feedback onto an interactive 3D anatomical interface, allowing crew members to visually inspect stress points, bone density shifts, and recommended countermeasures without needing assistance from Earth-based flight surgeons.

What benefits does it have?

100% Offline Autonomy: Operates completely locally without external API keys or internet connectivity, ensuring zero downtime during deep-space communication blackouts or high-latency periods (such as Mars missions).

Data Privacy & Security: Because all processing and vector retrieval occur locally on edge hardware, sensitive astronaut medical telemetry never leaves the spacecraft.

Proactive Countermeasure Guidance: Rather than waiting for post-mission evaluations, astronauts receive immediate, actionable insights (such as targeted resistive exercise adjustments or nutritional interventions) to slow down microgravity-induced bone and muscle loss in real time.

What is the intended impact of the project?

As humanity transitions from Low Earth Orbit (LEO) to deep-space exploration—such as Lunar Gateway and crewed Mars missions—communication delays of up to 20+ minutes each way make real-time telemedicine from Earth impossible. Galden bridges this gap by turning the spacecraft into an autonomous medical diagnostic hub. Its intended impact is to safeguard astronaut health, prevent irreversible musculoskeletal damage during multi-year missions, and provide a scalable edge-AI medical framework that can also be adapted for remote, low-connectivity environments on Earth (such as polar research stations, submarines, or disaster zones).

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

(Adjust any specific libraries or frameworks below to match your exact codebase)

Programming Languages: Python (for AI orchestration, data processing, and backend logic), JavaScript / TypeScript (for the interactive frontend and 3D rendering).

AI & Data Architecture: Local edge-deployed language models, quantized vector databases for fast offline retrieval, and multi-agent reinforcement learning/reasoning workflows trained and validated against open-source biomedical datasets (NASA Open Science Data Repository [OSDR], NASA Human Research Program [HRP], and NIH literature).

3D Visualization & UI: WebGL / Three.js (or React Three Fiber) for rendering the interactive 3D bio-telemetry model.

Development & Testing Environment: Developed and benchmarked across Windows and Linux environments using local GPU acceleration to ensure smooth, low-latency offline inference.

How is your project creative?

Bridging Molecular Biology with Spatial 3D UI: Most health trackers display raw numbers or flat line graphs. Galden translates complex cellular and biochemical mechanisms (like osteoblast/osteoclast activity and sclerostin expression) into an intuitive, visual 3D diagnostic interface that astronauts can grasp at a glance.

Edge-Native Multi-Agent Collaboration: Rather than using a single monolithic chatbot, Galden simulates a team of specialized medical and physiological agents debating and verifying telemetry data entirely offline—bringing hospital-grade diagnostic reasoning into a self-contained, zero-internet environment.

What factors did your team consider?

Deep-Space Communication Constraints: We designed the entire stack around the reality of communication blackouts and latency, strictly eliminating external cloud dependencies and API keys.

Compute & Resource Efficiency: Spacecraft have strict power and hardware limits. We prioritized lightweight, quantized local models and efficient vector storage so the software runs reliably on edge hardware without overloading onboard systems.

Scientific & Biological Accuracy: Rather than treating spaceflight health generically, our research focused on specific, documented spaceflight pathologies—grounding the system's logic in real NASA physiological datasets and bone-remodeling pathways.

Usability Under Stress: In high-stress environments, astronauts need clarity, not clutter. We designed the 3D interface to highlight critical anomalies immediately while keeping deeper diagnostic logs accessible on demand.
